_comment: THE THREE-BAND PAYLOAD POLICY. Replaces the single hard ceiling on the two gzip figures that measure bytes-to-first-move. The owner's call, in his words: "wrt ceiling, it's a soft ceiling, moore an indication so let's add another rule like, target is <300k, but we take action when it reaches >400k otherwise, small additions are ok as functionality improves right? i think that's a great way to go about things long term since the app will inevitably add more features and progress, but we want to avoid bloating too much makes sense?" BANDS: value <= target is a silent pass; target < value <= action WARNS and passes (it is an indication, not a gate); value > action is a hard fail; and delta > delta_cap is a hard fail whatever the absolute figure. THE DELTA CAP IS THE PART THAT DOES THE WORK - a flat 'act at 400k' lets one commit add 70,000 bytes and pass in silence, which is exactly the fat-wire regression the ceiling was built to catch. WHAT `baseline` IS: the last measurement somebody ACCEPTED, not the previous commit - nothing in CI or in a local build can measure a previous ref without rebuilding it (~11 min). So the cap reads 'growth since the last accepted checkpoint'. Growth therefore accumulates: three innocent +2,000 ships against a 5,000 cap turn the THIRD one red. That is the policy asking for a checkpoint every ~5,000 bytes of drift, not an accusation. HOW TO MOVE A BASELINE, and the only way it ever moves: `python3 scripts/check_payload_budget.py --accept-baseline <metric> --reason "..."`. It refuses a figure already over the action threshold, and it records the previous value, the ref, the date and the reason, so this file is a growth log. NEVER AUTOMATIC: a gate that rewrote its own baseline on every green run would make the delta always 0 and the cap vacuous while still reading as a check that ran - CLAUDE.md §6.6's failure class reached the long way round. A SELF-ADVANCING BASELINE IS A DELTA CHECK THAT NEVER RUNS. A MISSING baseline is a HARD FAIL, not a skip, for the same reason, and both gates print how many metrics reached a verdict. target/action/delta_cap are HAND-SET here, with reasoning in each metric's _comment; there is no flag for them, and --update says so out loud rather than silently declining. The band logic lives twice (scripts/_payload_policy.py for the python gate, scripts/_payload_policy.js for the browser gate) and tests/payload_policy.test.mjs pins the two equal over tests/artifacts/payload_policy_cases.json. THE TWO METRICS ARE ON DIFFERENT SCALES AND DO NOT SHARE NUMBERS: the eager set is the neural payload alone; first_hand is that plus the shared Quartz bundles plus whichever per-node chunks the pinned start draw pulls.

neural.eager_gzip_bytes.measured_from: source/public/static/neural, minus the on-demand chunk dirs and the DEFERRED list, each file gzipped separately (measure_neural)
neural.eager_gzip_bytes.baseline_reason: Dev's own level BEFORE the v1.219.0 camera change (orchestrator CAM-GO0, owner pre-authorisation 2026-09-29), so that change's +2,218 B stays its PR's visible delta. Measured on this branch's tree with dev 45d114a10's own neural.js/neural.css (sandbox build of origin/dev neural/, CSS byte-identical): 342,998 B, +2,983 B over the 340,015 B accepted at v1.216.0 (8947416e0). The PRs that moved it since that accept, on dev's first-parent history: #259, #260, #261, #262 (videos row arrows), #263 (outcome on cards), #265 (card click contract), #266, #268, #267 (win-chance latency). Target, action and delta_cap untouched.
neural.eager_gzip_bytes._comment: TARGET 300,000 is the owner's figure verbatim ('target is <300k'). Measured at v1.188.2 the eager set is ~329,800, so this metric SITS IN THE WARN BAND ON ARRIVAL and is expected to keep warning until the payload is trimmed. That is intended - a target is an aspiration you are measured against, not a line you are currently inside - but it is worth saying plainly, because a gate that warns on every single run is a gate people learn to scroll past. ACTION 400,000 is the owner's figure verbatim, and it is ~70,000 above today: on the tree this policy was written against the OLD hard ceiling was 330,000 against a measured 329,808, i.e. 192 BYTES of headroom, so the next neural feature of any size was going red on arrival. DELTA CAP 5,000 is the number that keeps the 70,000 of new room honest. It is ~1.5% of the current figure and ~2.6x the largest ordinary single-ship growth on record (the three measured neural.js bumps in budget_neural.json's history: +626, +1,929, +581 gzip), so an ordinary feature never trips it; and it is 14x smaller than the 70,000 cliff it exists to catch. RECOMPUTE THE CURRENT FIGURE: `npm run validate:payload` prints it, or `python3 scripts/check_payload_budget.py` after a build.
neural.eager_gzip_bytes.baseline_source: measured from the built tree by this script

first_hand_gzip_bytes.measured_from: every localhost byte the page requested before the first [data-tech] card existed, gzipped per response
first_hand_gzip_bytes.baseline_reason: PR B2 (v1.216.0, origin coherence: 95 listings deal their own outcome table), accepted BEFORE its capture under the owner's standing pre-authorisation (OCPRB4, confirmed OCQ6B: his 2026-09-29 'both increase the cap and trim it too', read as moving the accepted baseline, never widening target, action or delta_cap): each feature records its own acceptance. First-hand core +7,590 B gzip against PR 233's accepted 351,963 (v1.209.0), measured by e2e/journeys/payload-first-hand.spec.ts (start K-Guard Top, 11 requests). The same page build with dev 15a71060e's own emit and bundle (built from its own sources) swapped in reads 355,607, so +3,644 is dev's own drift since that acceptance, never re-accepted, and +3,946 is this PR: graph-data.json +3,925 (cal.at, the 95 listing tables, and absentAt, the 4 masked-state absences, by the spec's zlib-9) and curriculum.json +21 (the score weights the tables re-weight); every other request is byte-identical. Measured on static/neural emitted from this branch's merged tree 8947416e0 (keyless), over the fc97b06ce page build. Accepted so the next change gets its full 6,000 B per-change room back; target, action and delta_cap untouched.
first_hand_gzip_bytes._comment: DERIVED FROM THIS METRIC'S OWN FIGURE, NOT COPIED FROM THE EAGER SET - the two are on different scales and sharing numbers would be a mistake in both directions (a 400,000 action threshold here would leave ~13,000 of room against a measured 387,117, which is nothing). THE DERIVATION: first_hand = the eager set as actually requested + the shared Quartz bundles + the boot's per-node chunks. Measured at v1.188.2: shared bundles /postscript.js 27,776 + /index.css 9,896 + / 7,590 + /prescript.js 1,181 = 46,443 gzip locally, ~47,500 on a deploy (the PostHog snippet is injected into postscript.js and adds ~1,060 gzip) -> call it 48,000; per-node chunks at the p95 of their own size distribution, 3 decks + 1 dossier, = 3x3,370 + 6,741 = 16,851 -> call it 17,000. So this metric's bands are the eager set's bands plus 65,000: TARGET 300,000 + 65,000 = 365,000, ACTION 400,000 + 65,000 = 465,000. Sanity check against reality: measured 386,367 gzip locally / 387,117 in CI, so it arrives ~21,000 into the warn band (the eager set arrives ~30,000 into its own) and has ~78,000 of room before action. DELTA CAP 6,000, measured on first_hand_gzip_core_bytes: the total MINUS /postscript.js MINUS the per-node chunks, which are the two parts that move with no code change at all. 6,000 rather than the eager set's 5,000 because the core subtotal also counts /index.css and / (~17,500 gzip of Quartz-side surface that moves on template and stylesheet work the neural set never sees). Observed core growth on the last three ships: +8,254 (six versions, v1.177.0->v1.183.0), +2,747, +1,718 - so the first of those WOULD have asked for a checkpoint, correctly, since that is the window in which this payload ate its own ceiling twice. RECOMPUTE: `npx playwright test -c e2e/playwright.config.ts payload-first-hand` and read tests/artifacts/first_hand_payload.json. A LOCAL RUN IS ~1,060 B LIGHTER THAN CI on the TOTAL and identical on the CORE - that asymmetry is the whole reason the delta is measured on the core.
